questions.question: Who was the first Indian composer to win the Grammy Award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Ravi Shankar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar will be honoured with a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award posthumously, organizers of the Recording Academy announced, the first Indian to get the prestigious award.
 
• The award would be presented on February 10 at the 55th Grammy Awards ceremony in Los Angeles.
 
• Shankar was a true pioneer in introducing Indian music to the West, he said, adding the music icon influenced artists across classical, jazz, pop, rock, and world music genres, including the Beatles, John Coltrane, Philip Glass, and his daughters, Norah Jones and Anoushka Shankar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Grammy Award, any of a series of awards presented annually in the United States by the National Academy of Recording Arts & Sciences.

 
 
• Winners are selected from more than 25 fields, which cover such genres as pop, rock, rap, R&B, country, reggae, classical, gospel, and jazz, as well as production and postproduction work, including packaging and album notes.
 
 
 
• Anoushka Shankar is a British Indian sitar player and composer.
 
 
• She is the daughter of Pandit Ravi Shankar

questions.question: Which is the highest gallantry award during the war time in India?
questions.solution:
Param Vir Chakra is the highest gallantry award in India.

 
 

 
 
**Awards**

 
 
 
**Description**

 
 
 

 
 
Ashoka Chakra

 
 

 
 
 
It is awarded to armed forces, CAPFs, Railway Police and State Police.

 
 
 

 
 
__**Param Vir Chakra**__

 
 
 
__**It is awarded only to armed forces or person under the command of Armed forces.**__

 
 
 

 
 
Mahavir Chakra

 
 
 
It is awarded to members of the Indian armed forces who display great acts of gallantry during the war.

 
 
 

 
 
Bharat Ratna

 
 

 
 
 
It is awarded in recognition of exceptional service performance of the highest order in any field of human venture.

questions.question: Dr. MS Swaminathan was chosen for the Ramon Magsaysay award in which of the following year ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1971.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dr. Swaminathan received **the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1971.**
 
• Dr. M. S. Swaminathan was a renowned Indian agricultural scientist and a crucial figure in the** green revolution** globally.
 
• **He was a recipient of many national and international awards due to his significant contributions to the field of agriculture and plant genetics.**
 
• Among the prestigious awards he received was the Ramon Magsaysay Award, a notable international honor.
 
• The Ramon Magsaysay Award was presented to him specifically for community leadership.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Dr. MS Swaminathan was honoured with the following awards:**

 
 
• Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Award in 1961.
 
• Padma Shri in 1967.
 
• Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1971.
 
• Padma Bhushan in 1972.
 
• World Food Prize in 1987.
 
• Padma Vibhushan in 1989.
 
 
 
• **Notable works of M S Swaminathan are:**
 
 
• 50 Years of Green Revolution.
 
• An Evergreen Revolution.
 
• Wheat Revolution.
 
• Sustainable Agriculture: Towards Food Security.

questions.question: Arjuna Award was introduced in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1961**__.

• **Arjuna Award:-**

 
 
• The Arjuna Award is considered the second-highest sporting honor presented by the Government of India.
 
• It is given in recognition of outstanding achievement in Sports.
 
• The award is named after Arjuna, one of the characters of the Sanskrit epic Mahabharata of ancient India.
 
• The Arjuna Awards were instituted in 1961 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
• They are awarded annually and include a statue of Arjuna, a certificate, and a cash prize.
 
• Numerous esteemed sportspersons have been recipients of these awards, such as Sachin Tendulkar (Cricket), Viswanathan Anand (Chess), P.V. Sindhu (Badminton), and M.C. Mary Kom (Boxing), among others

questions.question: Who is the first non-Indian to receive the Bharat Ratna ?
questions.solution:
The first non-Indian to receive the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, was** Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan**, also known as "Frontier Gandhi."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] __Important Points__

Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (1890–1988), affectionately known as "Bacha Khan" or "Badshah Khan," was a Pashtun leader and a staunch advocate for nonviolent resistance, closely allied with Mahatma Gandhi during the struggle for India's independence from British rule. Born in the Peshawar Valley in what is now Pakistan, his life and work were deeply rooted in the principles of nonviolence and social reform, making him a pivotal figure in the Indian independence movement, especially in the North-West Frontier Province (now Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan).

**Key Aspects of Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan's Work:**

 
• 
 
**Khudai Khidmatgars (Servants of God)**: Khan founded the Khudai Khidmatgars, also known as the "Red Shirts," in 1929. This was a nonviolent resistance movement composed mainly of Pashtuns committed to the cause of India’s independence. The movement also focused on social reform within the Pashtun community, advocating for education, women's rights, and the unity between Hindus and Muslims.

 
 
• 
 
**Nonviolent Resistance:** Drawing inspiration from Gandhi, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was a firm believer in nonviolence as the means to achieve independence. He and his followers faced brutal repression from the British authorities for their activities, enduring arrests, beatings, and massacres. Despite the violence unleashed upon them, they adhered to their nonviolent discipline.

 
 
• 
 
**Partition Opposition: **Khan was opposed to the partition of India, fearing the consequences for the Pashtuns and other Muslims who would find themselves on the wrong side of the border. He stood for a united India, where Muslims, Hindus, and people of all religions could coexist peacefully.

 
 
• 
 
**Life After Independence: **Post-independence, Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan found himself in the newly created Pakistan. He continued his struggle for the rights of Pashtuns and was frequently imprisoned for his opposition to Pakistani government policies. His commitment to nonviolence and his advocacy for the rights of his people remained unwavering throughout his life.

 
 
• 
 
**Legacy: **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan's legacy is that of a towering figure in the history of nonviolent struggle, likened to Gandhi in his commitment to peace and justice. He left behind a lasting impact on the Indian subcontinent's social and political landscape, remembered for his courage, conviction, and dedication to the principles of nonviolence and communal harmony.

 

Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan passed away in 1988 in Peshawar, Pakistan, but his message of peace and nonviolence continues to inspire movements for social justice and peace around the world. In recognition of his contributions to the Indian independence movement and his lifelong commitment to nonviolence, he was awarded the Bharat Ratna by the Government of India in 1987, becoming the first non-Indian to receive this highest civilian honor.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win the Nobel Prize?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**Rabindranath Tagore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian to win the Nobel Prize**__.

 __
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian to get a Nobel Prize in 1913 for his work in **Literature**.
 
• He won the award for "his profoundly sensitive, fresh and beautiful verse, by which, with consummate skill, he has made his poetic thought, expressed in his own English words, a part of the literature of the West".
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Esther Duflo, Abhijit Banerjee, and Michael Kremer** were awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics in 2019.

 
 
• They were awarded "for their experimental approach to alleviating global poverty".
 
• Esther Duflo is the youngest person to be awarded the Nobel prize in economics.
 
 
 
• Gerty Theresa Cori was the third woman to win a Nobel Prize in science.
 
 
• She is the first woman to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for her vital role in the "discovery of the course of the catalytic conversion of glycogen". 
 
 
 
• Maria Goeppert Mayer got the Nobel prize in Physics for proposing the nuclear shell model of the atomic nucleus.
 
 
• She was the second woman to win a Nobel Prize in physics.
 
• The first was Marie Curie.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Nobel Prize in Physics for the year 2020 was awarded to three astrophysicists Roger Penrose from the UK, Reinhard Genzel from Germany, and Andrea Ghez from the USA.
 
• Emmanuelle Charpentier of France and Jennifer A Doudna of the USA have been awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing CRISPR/Cas9 genetic scissors, one of gene technology’s sharpest tools.
 
• The 2020 Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded to the World Food Programme (WFP), a United Nations (UN) agency, for its efforts to combat hunger, bettering conditions for peace in conflict-affected areas, and preventing the use of hunger as a weapon of war and conflict.
 
• American economists, Paul Milgrom, and Robert Wilson have been awarded the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences, 2020 for their work on commercial auctions.
 
• The Nobel Prize in Literature 2020 has been awarded to the USA poet Louise Glück "for her unmistakable poetic voice that with austere beauty makes individual existence universal."

questions.question: The National Bravery Awards is presented annually to children on the eve of________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __**2**__ i.e __**Republic Day**__.

__
 
• The **National Bravery Awards were started by the Indian Council for Child Welfare in 1957**__.
 
• It was awarded to recognize children for outstanding deeds of bravery and meritorious service and to inspire others to emulate their example.
 
• **The National Bravery Awards is presented annually to children on the eve of __Republic Day__.**
 
• 22 children, including 10 girls and 12 boys, had received the National Bravery Award on January 26, 2020.
 
• President **Jair Bolsonaro** was the Republic Day parade chief guest of 2020.
